extra.message: User-controlled search parameters (decrypted from the client-supplied 'q' POST parameter via getParameters()) are substituted directly into a raw SQL template string using regex replaceAll (lines 180-183), and the resulting string is executed with Statement.executeQuery() (line 186) instead of a PreparedStatement. An attacker who knows/derives the per-session AES key (exposed to the client, see getEncryptKey()) can submit arbitrary key:value pairs that are placed verbatim between the LIKE '%...%' quotes, allowing classic SQL injection (e.g. closing the quote and injecting UNION SELECT or boolean/time-based payloads) against the PRODUCTS/PRODUCTTYPES tables.

getQueryString() concatenates the raw key/value pairs decrypted from the attacker-controlled 'q' parameter (see getParameters(), lines 141-162) directly into a string with no HTML encoding. This string is documented/used for a 'You searched for:' display on the page, so any HTML/script characters an attacker places in the decrypted key or value are reflected unescaped into the response, enabling reflected XSS.

getJSON() and getTrHTML() build the HTML table rows and JSON response by directly concatenating the product/desc/type/price fields with no HTML or JSON string escaping. Because these values are sourced from a query that is itself vulnerable to SQL injection (AdvancedSearch.setResults(), AdvancedSearch.java lines 172-186), an attacker can use a UNION-based injection to make arbitrary attacker-chosen strings (including '<script>' markup or characters that break out of the JSON string) appear in these fields, which are then written unescaped into the HTML page or JSON consumed by client-side JS, resulting in stored/reflected XSS.

isDebug() gates verbose debug output solely on an unauthenticated, client-supplied 'debug' request parameter with no permission check. When true, getDebugOutput() (lines 79-86) returns the full raw SQL statements (both before and after parameter substitution, including any injected content, added at lines 178 and 185) plus complete exception stack traces (added in the catch blocks at lines 158-160, 204-207) for display on the page. Any anonymous user can request ?debug=true to obtain internal SQL query text and stack traces, aiding further SQL injection exploitation and leaking internal implementation details.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
